pageCache.text:

Instagram

Mission, Vision & Values
Meadow High School Learning For Life
We aim to deliver high-quality personalised education to young people aged 11 – 19 in the Hillingdon area, empowering them to leave Meadow High School with PURPOSE and CHOICE over their futures.
This is summarised in our strap line: ‘Learning for Life’
Belong, Believe, Become
Our 5 Year VISION
An EXCEPTIONAL SCHOOL to work and be educated at
We have no idea how good we can be but..
We aspire to be a high-performing organisation where:
Parents and young people want to be educated here, as it is the best & most appropriate place to be educated.
ALL students leave Meadow with PURPOSE & CHOICE over their future because they have:
Relevant & Appropriate Qualifications
Character to contribute
Appointment at Meadow is not the pinnacle of a colleague's career but the start of something much bigger.
We constantly strive to improve
Meadow High School is shaping the education system locally and nationally.
Meadow High School is Ofsted exceptional by placing the interests of our students, staff & wider community at the heart of everything we do.
Student Friendly Version of Values
Motivation - Is motivated and open to challenge and improve, individually and collectively
Excellence - Has high standards and demonstrates manners, honesty and integrity
Achievement - Achieves in academic, artistic, sporting and cultural forms
Dedication - Shows commitment and kindness towards self, students, staff and the wider community
Opportunities - Uses available opportunities to help them to grow
Willingness - Works kindly, collaboratively & creatively for the good of everyone
Underpinned by our CORE PRINCIPLES
Delivered through our PROCESSES

Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to Meadow High School
It is an incredible honour to be the Headteacher of Meadow High School. Meadow High School has amazing students, an experienced and dedicated staff and state-of-the-art facilities spread across two sites, Royal Lane and Northwood Road. Our school is growing in size and is over subscribed as we are seen to be fulfilling our Mission to
‘Deliver high quality personalised education to young people aged 11 – 19 in the Hillingdon area, empowering them to leave Meadow High School with PURPOSE and CHOICE over their futures’
I have high expectations of all the students who attend our school and I will always put them first, as they only get one chance for a World-class education. Whatever path they choose when they leave us, it is our role to ensure that students leave Meadow High School ready to contribute to the communities they are a part of. This is summarised in our strap line ‘Learning for Life’.
To achieve this, a student needs to leave school with relevant and appropriate qualifications, skills, knowledge and personal qualities. Meadow offers a broad, inclusive curriculum which enables all students to succeed through a range of academic and vocational courses and an extensive extracurricular programme. We share and celebrate student successes inside and outside the classroom so that students truly ‘Belong, Believe and Become’ during enjoyable years at Meadow High School.
We are a values-driven, supportive community, and we ensure we get to know our students as individuals. Relationships are central in making this happen and students and staff frequently go the extra mile for one another. I am privileged to serve such a great community and I look forward to working with you all in the future.
Graham Cunningham Headteacher Meadow High School
Graham Cunningham Headteacher

Out of Hours Safeguarding Contact Information / Reporting a Safeguarding Concern
Worried about a child out of school hours?
If a child is in immediate danger or at risk of immediate harm, you should contact the Police on 999
If you are concerned about a child you should share your concern with our local Children’s Social Care Service by calling Hillingdon Children's Services/Stronger Families Hub on 01895 556006 or email StrongerFamiliesHub@hillingdon.gov.uk
You can also contact the NSPCC for advice on 0808 800 5000 or email help@NSPCC.org.uk
If you have non-urgent information about the safety or welfare of a child to share with the safeguarding team at Meadow High School then please contact the relevant Safeguarding Designated Lead listed on our Safeguarding page, and below. You can also email meadow@meadowhighschool.org
If you need an immediate response or if you are concerned for a child’s immediate safety or welfare please contact the Police.
Reporting a Safeguarding Concern
The safety and wellbeing of our pupils is at the heart of everything we do at Meadow High School.
If you have any safeguarding concerns you can report these in one of the following ways:
Safeguarding Leads
Designated Safeguarding Lead:
Mr G Cunningham (Headteacher)
Deputy Designated Safeguarding Leads: Mrs H O'Neill (Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead - Northwood Road Campus) Miss N Sohun (Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead - Royal Lane Campus) Mrs A Fabisch (Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead - Royal Lane Campus)
You can contact the Safeguarding Leads at Meadow High School in the following ways:
by telephone: (01895 443310)
by email: meadow@meadowhighschool.org
Other useful contacts:
National support organisations
Their counsellors can support young people 24 hours a day. Call them on 0800 1111.
Advice and guidance; there is also a page where you can pass on information about crime anonymously.
Support and opportunities for young people, particularly young people who are moving away from gangs and crime. They have helped thousands of young people.

Personal Belongings
All personal belongings should be clearly marked with the owner's name.
Any valuables should be handed in to the class tutor for safe keeping and to the PE staff before a games lesson.
Valuable items, such as MP3 players, I-pods, must not be brought into school.
If mobile phones are brought to school, they must be turned off and handed in to the class tutor at Registration, for safekeeping.
Parents should note that the school cannot accept responsibility for the loss or damage to personal property. Anything found should be handed in to a member of staff or the office.
UNIFORM & BELONGINGS
Students are not encouraged to wear jewellery, but may wear a watch and small earrings (studs only) and any items relating to the students religion, e.g. cross and chain, metal karha, etc. Please note: in the interests of safety, other items of jewellery are not to be worn in school.
We would strongly recommend that any items of value are not worn at school, as we cannot accept responsibility for loss or damage to property.
LOST PROPERTY
PLEASE ENSURE ALL ITEMS OF UNIFORM, PE KIT AND PROPERTY ARE CLEARLY LABELLED WITH YOUR CHILD'S NAME. It is much easier to locate a lost item if it is labelled. Thank you.

Governors
Welcome to Meadow High School Governing Body
The school's Governing Body has a strategic role in the development of the school and is responsible for its policies and finances but does not become involved in day-to-day management issues; that is the role of the headteacher. Governors ensure key priorities are included in the school development plan (SDP) and then monitor progress towards completion.
Meadow governors are committed to providing a safe, challenging and stimulating environment to help pupils become confident young adults, maximising their abilities and developing their skills to allow them to be happy and contribute to society in their "Life Beyond Meadow”.
The Governing Body's responsibilities are:
The aim of all of these activities is to promote school improvement and to raise standards and achievement.
Child protection
Disciplinary procedures
Premises including health and safety
Admissions to the school
Information for parents, families and community
Members of Meadow High School Governing Body
All our governors are volunteers from the school's community who wish to make a positive contribution to our children's education.
There are twelve members:
The Governing Body has the authority to appoint Associate Governors as appropriate to provide additional support and expertise.
If you have any suggestions or questions for the Governing Body, please contact:
Clerk to the Governors: Mr Russell Carpenter rcarpenter@meadowhighschool.org
4 Parent Governors (elected by parents).

Pathway 2 - Sixth Form Leavers - Trip To Brighton
This week, our Key Stage 5 leavers enjoyed a fantastic trip to Brighton. We had an amazing day making the most of the sunshine and sea air, as well as enjoying the arcades, shops, funfair, ice cream, and traditional fish and chips on the beach.
It was a wonderful opportunity to celebrate the end of their school journey together and reflect on all they have achieved. You should all be incredibly proud of your accomplishments during your time at school. We wish each of you every success and happiness for the future. Good luck in your next adventures!
